tasks.question: Is there any situation where living in a city is not the better choice?

cues.cue: someone / needs / peace and quiet to work
models: Except in cases where someone needs peace and quiet to work, the rule generally applies that city life offers more opportunity, because most people value convenience over calm.

cues.cue: retirees / seeking / a slower pace of life
models: The one notable exception is retirees seeking a slower pace of life, which stands apart because their priorities shift away from career and convenience.

cues.cue: high housing costs
models: Aside from high housing costs, little else makes city life genuinely worse than the countryside, and as a result most drawbacks are outweighed by opportunity.

cues.cue: families wanting more space for children
models: Other than families wanting more space for children, there is little to distinguish why city life would be the wrong choice for most people.

cues.cue: extremely high-cost cities
models: With the exception of extremely high-cost cities, this holds true across the board, since most urban areas still offer better access to jobs and services.

cues.cue: a few overcrowded megacities
models: Barring a few overcrowded megacities, the situation remains largely positive, so city living continues to appeal to most young professionals.
